evidence.claim: Samsara reported Q1 FY27 results on June 4, 2026, including nearly $2 billion in ARR, 30% year-over-year ARR growth, $101 million in net-new ARR, $1.2 billion in ARR from customers above $100,000 ARR, 62% year-over-year ARR growth from customers above $1 million, more than 20% of net-new ACV from emerging products for a second consecutive quarter, and a third consecutive quarter of GAAP EPS profitability.
evidence.source_title: Samsara Approaches $2 Billion in ARR Amid Physical Economy Boom

evidence.claim: Samsara describes itself as the pioneer of the Connected Operations Platform and says tens of thousands of customers use it across transportation, construction, wholesale and retail trade, field services, logistics, manufacturing, utilities and energy, government, healthcare and education, food and beverage, and other physical operations sectors.
evidence.source_title: Samsara Approaches $2 Billion in ARR Amid Physical Economy Boom

evidence.claim: Samsara's FY26 release reported $1.9 billion in FY26 ARR, 30% year-over-year growth, $432 million in net-new ARR, $1.2 billion in ARR from customers above $100,000 ARR, and more than 25 trillion data points flowing through the platform annually.
evidence.source_title: Samsara’s FY26 Shows Accelerated Growth at Scale as AI Platform Delivers Clear Benefits to Organizations Powering the Global Economy

evidence.claim: Samsara's large operational dataset and continued large-customer expansion support the hypothesis that it could become a physical-world AI workflow layer, but the evidence does not yet prove that AI features independently drive pricing power or retention.
evidence.source_title: Samsara’s FY26 Shows Accelerated Growth at Scale as AI Platform Delivers Clear Benefits to Organizations Powering the Global Economy

memory_update.text: IOT maps to edge operational data and industrial AI data nodes as a speculative-shadow second-order AI candidate; current official evidence supports strong ARR growth, large-customer expansion, emerging-product contribution, and a large proprietary physical-operations dataset, but not yet standalone AI monetization.

PATH maps to enterprise AI automation and agentic workflow orchestration nodes; official evidence supports product-level agentic AI positioning, AI-agent security certification, and Azure AI Foundry integration, but the chokepoint thesis remains unproven until ARR acceleration and retention effects are visible.

For IOT, next layer should separate base connected-operations growth from AI-driven incremental economics by tracking emerging-products ACV mix, AI product attach rate, net retention, product gross margin, and customer expansion case studies.

For PATH, next layer should test whether agentic automation is reviving the RPA growth curve or merely slowing decline by reviewing Q1 FY27 official disclosures, AI deal mix, AI expansion deal size, customer production deployments, churn, and competitive displacement data.

Neither IOT nor PATH should be promoted as a Serenity bottleneck candidate until primary filings or transcripts show AI-specific revenue pull-through, pricing power, retention lift, or workflow lock-in that cannot be easily replicated by larger software platforms.

summary: Layer 2B maps two speculative-shadow software names to second-order AI/automation nodes rather than primary AI infrastructure chokepoints. Samsara has stronger current evidence for AI-adjacent operating traction because Q1 FY27 and FY26 disclosures show rapid ARR growth, large-customer expansion, emerging-product contribution, Operational AI positioning, and a proprietary physical-operations data asset. UiPath has direct agentic-automation product evidence and certification/partnership signals, but the relationship remains more contested because AI adoption must translate into durable ARR acceleration, retention, and competitive insulation versus platform vendors. Neither ticker should be treated as a Serenity chokepoint yet; both require revenue-level proof that AI features create incremental pricing, retention, or workflow lock-in.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether Samsara's AI features materially improve pricing, product attach, customer retention, and cross-sell rather than simply supporting the existing connected-operations platform narrative.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review Q1 FY27 transcript, FY27 investor presentation, product-level disclosures, net retention trends, emerging-products ARR mix, and customer case studies showing AI-driven expansions.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Samsara maps to the physical-operations data layer: fleet, safety, equipment, and operational telemetry become training and workflow inputs for Operational AI. The potential bottleneck is not compute supply but proprietary, continuously refreshed edge data from asset-heavy industries.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify vertical-by-vertical AI adoption and whether infrastructure, construction, energy, and logistics customers are expanding because of AI use cases such as safety, maintenance, routing, and labor productivity.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Collect customer expansion examples, compare AI-product penetration across large accounts, and test whether emerging products maintain more than 20% of net-new ACV in later FY27 quarters.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Samsara is a second-order AI beneficiary candidate because its Connected Operations Cloud captures operational data from transportation, construction, logistics, manufacturing, utilities, energy, government, healthcare, and other physical-economy verticals. This could make it a vertical AI workflow layer for asset-heavy enterprises.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether agentic automation products drive ARR acceleration, larger deal sizes, higher net retention, and reduced churn, rather than acting as a repositioning label for slower-growth RPA.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review Q1 FY27 official earnings release and transcript, quantify AI-included deal mix, track ARR growth versus guidance, and compare customer wins against Microsoft, ServiceNow, Salesforce, and internal automation stacks.
ticker_relationships.relationship: UiPath maps to enterprise agentic automation and process orchestration: AI agents may increase demand for governed workflow execution, legacy application integration, document intelligence, and human-in-the-loop controls. The key question is whether RPA becomes an enabling layer for AI agents or is displaced by broader enterprise platforms.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify production deployment depth, not just pilots or product launches; look for multi-agent workflows running in regulated or mission-critical processes with measurable ROI.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check adoption of UiPath Maestro, Screen Agent, healthcare revenue-cycle products, AIUC-1 certification relevance, and evidence that agentic deployments expand beyond existing RPA customers.
ticker_relationships.relationship: UiPath has a plausible relationship to the agentic-workflow orchestration node because its platform combines robots, AI agents, process orchestration, document intelligence, governance, security, and enterprise integration. This creates a possible control-plane role between LLM agents and deterministic business-process execution.
